Incorrect. BaaS (backup as a service) is just another name for a cloud backup service. It handles electronic backup data, not storage of physical tapes.

questions.stem: Norm would like to conduct a disaster recovery test for his organization and wants to choose the most thorough type of test, recognizing that it may be quite disruptive. What type of test should Norm choose?
questions.explanation: During a full interruption test, the team takes down the primary site and confirms that the disaster recovery site is capable of handling regular operations. The full interruption test is the most thorough test but also the most disruptive. During a parallel test, the team actually activates the disaster recovery site for testing, but the primary site remains operational. The checklist review is the least disruptive type of disaster recovery test. During a checklist review, team members each review the contents of their disaster recovery checklists on their own and suggest any necessary changes. During a tabletop exercise, team members come together and walk through a scenario without making any changes to information systems.
optionNotes: Correct. A full interruption test takes the primary site down and proves the DR site can carry regular operations. It is the most thorough test and also the most disruptive, which matches what Norm wants.
Incorrect. A parallel test does activate the DR site, but the primary site keeps running. That makes it less disruptive and less thorough than a full interruption test.
Incorrect. In a tabletop exercise, the team meets to walk through a scenario without changing any information systems. It is low-impact and doesn't prove the DR site can actually take over.
Incorrect. A checklist review is the least disruptive DR test. Team members each review their own checklists and suggest changes, so it is the opposite of the most thorough option.

questions.stem: Ed is building a network that supports IPv6 but needs to connect it to an IPv4 network. What type of device should Ed place between the networks?
questions.explanation: Ed's best option is to install an IPv6 to IPv4 gateway that can translate traffic between the networks. A bridge would be appropriate for different types of networks, whereas a router would make sense if the networks were similar. A modern switch might be able to carry both types of traffic but wouldn't be much help translating between the two protocols.
optionNotes: Incorrect. A switch forwards frames at Layer 2; a modern one may carry both IPv4 and IPv6 traffic but does not translate between the two protocols.
Incorrect. A router connects similar networks using the same protocol. It does not translate IPv6 traffic into IPv4, which is what Ed needs.
Incorrect. A bridge links network segments that use different Layer 2 types. It does not convert IPv6 into IPv4.
Correct. A gateway translates between different protocols. An IPv6-to-IPv4 gateway converts traffic so the two networks can communicate.

questions.stem: Henry's company has deployed an extensive IoT infrastructure for building monitoring that includes environmental controls, occupancy sensors, and a variety of other sensors and controllers that help manage the building. Which of the following security concerns should Henry report as the most critical in his analysis of the IoT deployment?
options: The lack of local storage space for security logs that is common to IoT devices.
The IoT devices may not have a separate administrative interface, allowing anybody on the same network to attempt to log into them and making brute-force attacks possible.
The IoT devices may not support strong encryption for communications, exposing the log and sensor data to interception on the network.
The long-term support and patching model for the IoT devices may create security and operational risks for the organization.
questions.explanation: Henry's biggest concern should be the long-term security and supportability of the IoT devices. As these devices are increasingly embedded in buildings and infrastructure, the support model and security model are important to understand. Both the lack of separate administrative access and the lack of strong encryption can be addressed by placing the IoT devices on a dedicated subnet or network that prevents other users from accessing the devices directly. This will help limit the risk without undue expense or complexity and is a common practice. Finally, lack of storage space can be a concern but is not the most important when looking at the risks IoT devices can create.
optionNotes: Incorrect. IoT devices often have little local log storage, but that's a minor issue. Sending logs off the device solves it, and it isn't the most critical IoT risk.

Incorrect. A missing separate admin interface is a real weakness. Putting the IoT devices on their own subnet or network stops other users from reaching them directly, so this risk is cheap and easy to reduce.
Incorrect. Weak encryption is also reduced by isolating the devices on a dedicated network segment. That's a common, low-cost practice, so this isn't the top concern.

Correct. IoT devices built into buildings stay in place for years, and the vendor may stop supporting or patching them. That ongoing security and operational risk can't easily be fixed with network controls, so it's the most critical concern.

questions.stem: Isaac wants to use a connectionless protocol to transfer data because he needs to optimize the speed of transmission over reliability. Which protocol should he select?
questions.explanation: UDP, the User Datagram Protocol, is a connectionless, best-effort protocol that is often used when sending data quickly without strong requirements for reliability features like error correction and detection or flow control to make sense. TCP is connection-oriented and provides those and other reliability features. ICMP, the Internet Control Message Protocol, is used to check routes and paths as well as availability but is not used for significant data transfer in normal cases. SNMP is a network management monitoring protocol.
optionNotes: Incorrect. ICMP checks routes, paths and host availability (ping, traceroute). It isn't meant for moving significant amounts of data, so it isn't a transport choice here.
Incorrect. TCP is connection-oriented. It adds reliability features such as error detection and correction and flow control, which slow transmission. That is the opposite of what Isaac wants.
Correct. UDP is a connectionless, best-effort protocol. It skips error correction and flow control so it can send data quickly, which suits Isaac's choice of speed over reliability.
Incorrect. SNMP is a protocol for monitoring and managing network devices, not a general-purpose data transport protocol.

questions.stem: Which one of the following actions is not required under the EU General Data Protection Regulation?
options: Organizations must allow individuals to opt out of information sharing.
Organizations must provide individuals with lists of employees with access to information.
Organizations must use proper mechanisms to protect data against unauthorized disclosure.
Organizations must have a dispute resolution process for privacy issues.
questions.explanation: The EU General Data Protection Regulation does not require that organizations provide individuals with employee lists.
optionNotes: Incorrect. This is a real requirement. Under GDPR, individuals have choice and control over their data, including the right to object to or opt out of having their information shared. So it is not the answer to a 'not required' question.
Correct. GDPR gives individuals rights to access, correct and erase their data. It does not require organizations to hand over lists of the employees who can access that data.

Incorrect. This is a real requirement. GDPR's security principle requires appropriate technical and organizational measures, such as encryption or pseudonymization, to protect personal data from unauthorized disclosure.

Incorrect. This is a real requirement. GDPR requires ways to enforce privacy and resolve complaints, such as letting individuals complain to supervisory authorities and seek remedies, so a dispute resolution process is expected.

questions.stem: Tammy is selecting a disaster recovery facility for her organization. She would like to choose a facility that balances the time required to recover operations with the cost involved. What type of facility should she choose?
questions.explanation: Tammy should choose a warm site. This type of facility meets her requirements for a good balance between cost and recovery time. It is less expensive than a hot site but facilitates faster recovery than a cold site. A red site is not a type of disaster recovery facility.
optionNotes: Incorrect. A hot site recovers fastest because it's fully equipped and kept current, but it's the most expensive option. That fails the cost side of the balance Tammy wants.
Correct. A warm site costs less than a hot site and recovers faster than a cold site. That makes it the balance between recovery time and cost that Tammy is looking for.
Incorrect. A cold site is the cheapest option, but recovery takes the longest because equipment and data have to be brought in and set up. It doesn't balance time against cost.
Incorrect. "Red site" isn't a recognized type of disaster recovery facility. It's a distractor.

questions.stem: What layer of the OSI model is associated with datagrams?
questions.explanation: When data reaches the Transport layer, it is sent as segments (TCP) or datagrams (UDP). Above the Transport layer, data becomes a data stream, while below the Transport layer, they are converted to packets at the Network layer, frames at the Data Link layer, and bits at the Physical layer.
optionNotes: Incorrect. The Session layer, like the other upper layers, handles data as a data stream. It does not use datagrams, which start at the Transport layer.
Correct. At the Transport layer, data is sent as segments when TCP is used and as datagrams when UDP is used, so this is the layer tied to datagrams.
Incorrect. At the Network layer (Layer 3), data is called packets, not datagrams.
Incorrect. At the Data Link layer (Layer 2), data is grouped into frames, not datagrams.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is not a valid key length for the Advanced Encryption Standard?
questions.explanation: The Advanced Encryption Standard supports encryption with 128-bit keys, 192-bit keys, and 256-bit keys.
optionNotes: Incorrect. 128 bits is a valid AES key length. It is the smallest of the three AES key sizes and uses 10 rounds of encryption, so it can't be the answer.
Incorrect. 192 bits is a valid AES key length. It is the middle of the three supported sizes and uses 12 rounds, so it can't be the answer.
Incorrect. 256 bits is a valid AES key length. It is the strongest key size AES supports and uses 14 rounds, so it can't be the answer.
Correct. AES supports only 128-, 192- and 256-bit keys, so a 384-bit key is not valid. 384 is a number you see with SHA-384 and ECC curves, which is why it can sound plausible.

questions.stem: Which one of the following technologies provides a function interface that allows developers to directly interact with systems without knowing the implementation details of that system?
questions.explanation: An application programming interface (API) allows developers to create a direct method for other users to interact with their systems through an abstraction that does not require knowledge of the implementation details. Access to object models, source code, and data dictionaries also indirectly facilitates interaction but does so in a manner that provides other developers with implementation details.
optionNotes: Incorrect. A data dictionary is a central catalog of data element definitions and relationships. It can help others work with a system indirectly, but it exposes implementation details instead of hiding them behind an abstract interface.

Incorrect. An object model describes a system's classes, objects and how they relate. Sharing it helps other developers, but it reveals internal design details rather than giving them a function interface that hides the implementation.

Incorrect. Source code is the implementation itself. Having it lets developers interact with a system only by understanding its internals, which is the opposite of an abstraction that hides implementation details.
Correct. An API is an abstraction layer of defined functions or calls. It lets developers and other systems interact with a system directly without knowing how that system is implemented.

questions.stem: Ian wants to assess the security of his company's new SaaS provider. Which of the following options is the most likely option that he can realistically expect to be able to use to assess a major cloud provider's security?
options: Run a vulnerability scan against the provider's external services.
Request a SOC 2 Type II report.
Run a vulnerability scan against the provider's internal systems.
Request a SOC 1 Type II report.
questions.explanation: Ian's best bet is a SOC report, and a SOC 2 Type II report will assess security controls and their application over time, telling him if the organization is responsibly maintaining their security efforts. A SOC 1 report looks at financial controls, and a Type I report only looks at how controls are described, not their application over time. Ian is unlikely to be allowed to run a vulnerability scan against a major provider's infrastructure either internally or externally.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Major cloud providers rarely allow customers to scan their externally facing infrastructure, so this is not a realistic way for Ian to assess the provider.
Correct. A SOC 2 Type II report assesses security controls and how they operated over a period of time. Major providers routinely share these reports with customers.
Incorrect. Ian will almost certainly not get access to scan a major provider's internal systems. This option is even less realistic than an external scan.
Incorrect. A SOC 1 report covers internal controls over financial reporting, not security controls, so it doesn't answer Ian's security question.

questions.stem: Sharon wants to conduct a pass-the-hash attack. Which of the following is not a common means of acquiring NTLM hashes for the attack?
options: Downloading the hashes from a third-party site
questions.explanation: Pass-the-hash attacks (PtH) often rely on dumped local account databases (the SAM), capturing credentials from the network while they are in transit or from active memory. Pass-the-hash attacks are not typically conducted by downloading hashes from third-party sites.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Dumping the local SAM database is a standard way to get NTLM hashes for local accounts, which an attacker can then replay in a pass-the-hash attack. That makes it a common method, so it's not the answer.
Incorrect. Tools such as Mimikatz pull cached credentials and NTLM hashes out of active memory (LSASS). This is one of the most common ways to gather hashes for PtH, so it's not the answer.
Incorrect. An attacker can capture NTLM authentication exchanges as they cross the network and take hashes from them. Because this is a recognized way to collect hashes, it's not the answer.

Correct. PtH needs the hash of a specific account on the target environment, and third-party sites don't provide those. Downloading hashes from such sites isn't a typical way to get material for a pass-the-hash attack.

questions.stem:
Match each one of the numbered protocols with the most accurate lettered description. Use each answer exactly once.
Protocol:
1. TCP
2. UDP
3. DNS
4. ARP

(Arrange the options in the order of the numbered items 1–4.)
options: Performs translations between MAC addresses and IP addresses
Performs translations between FQDNs and IP addresses
Transports data over a network in a connection-oriented fashion
Transports data over a network in a connectionless fashion
questions.explanation:
The protocols match with the descriptions as follows:
1. TCP: C. Transports data over a network in a connection-oriented fashion
2. UDP: D. Transports data over a network in a connectionless fashion
3. DNS: B. Performs translations between FQDNs and IP addresses
4. ARP: A. Performs translations between MAC addresses and IP addresses
The Domain Name System (DNS) translates human-friendly fully qualified domain names (FQDNs) into IP addresses, making it possible to easily remember websites and hostnames. ARP is used to resolve IP addresses into MAC addresses. TCP and UDP are used to control the network traffic that travels between systems. TCP does so in a connection-oriented fashion using the three-way handshake, while UDP uses connectionless “best-effort” delivery.
optionNotes: Goes with item 4 (ARP). ARP resolves IP addresses to MAC addresses so frames can be delivered on the local network segment.
Goes with item 3 (DNS). DNS translates human-friendly FQDNs into IP addresses, which makes hostnames and websites easy to remember.
Goes with item 1 (TCP). TCP is connection-oriented: it sets up a session with the three-way handshake before sending data.
Goes with item 2 (UDP). UDP is connectionless and gives best-effort delivery, with no handshake and no guarantee that data arrives.
